title: Questions about family sessions

questions.q: What if my child won't cooperate?
questions.a: Then we photograph what they're actually doing. Children don't have to perform for this to work — some of the best frames come from a kid who's climbing on their dad or whispering something ridiculous to their mom. I'd rather have that than seven people staring at the lens with the same tight smile.

questions.q: What should I tell my child beforehand?
questions.a: Something low-key, like: we're going to the park and Julie is going to take some pictures while we hang out and play. Try to avoid building it up into a big event, and skip the pre-session bribes and warnings. Kids arrive tense when they know they're being graded.

questions.q: My child is autistic, very shy, has sensory needs, or needs extra time. Is that okay?
questions.a: Absolutely. You don't need to share anything you're uncomfortable sharing, but if there's something that helps your child feel more comfortable or communicate more easily, let me know so I can adapt the session.

questions.q: Will you post photographs of my children online?
questions.a: Only with your written permission. You're welcome to keep your session completely private, and children's names and ages are never published anywhere — not on the website, not on social media, not in anything I print. Nothing from your gallery goes public until you've signed a release saying it can.

questions.q: What if we need to reschedule?
questions.a: Life with young children doesn't cooperate with a calendar. Fevers turn up the night before, someone doesn't sleep, the morning falls apart for reasons nobody could have predicted. I've raised young kids myself, and I'd far rather move your session than photograph a child who feels awful. With at least 24 hours' notice we'll find another date, no trouble at all. If something happens the morning of, just tell me as soon as you can and we'll work it out.

questions.q: What if a toddler needs a snack or a break?
questions.a: That's normal and it's not a problem. Bring a snack, a drink, wipes, a favorite toy or blanket, and a backup outfit if you want one. Just go easy on anything that stains right before we start. Breaks aren't lost time.

Yes. Please keep them leashed and bring waste bags and treats. If you'd like some family photographs without the dog, bring someone who can hold them for a few minutes. Leashes can often be edited out.

questions.q: There are more than seven of us. What do we do?
questions.a: Get in touch before you book so we can talk through timing and where we'd shoot. Regular pricing usually still applies, but a larger group needs a bit of planning.

questions.q: We're a blended family. Is that going to be awkward?
questions.a: Not at all. Blended, divorced, step and every other kind of family are welcome here. Just tell me who's important to photograph and any groupings you want, and I'll handle it without making it a thing.

questions.q: What time of day is best?
questions.a: Morning, or the couple of hours before sunset, when the light gets softer. Available times show up in the booking calendar, and I keep midday off the schedule in summer because overhead sun is unkind to everyone.

questions.q: Do we all have to match?
questions.a: Please don't. Coordinate instead — start with a few things you already own and like, build a loose palette around them, and mix solids with a pattern or two. There's more on this in Prepare for Your Session.
